title: MacroCoachGUI
summary: A desktop dashboard for tracking nutrition, weight, and fitness trends.
description: MacroCoachGUI is a Java Swing desktop application I built to make my MacroCoachAPI easier to use. It brings nutrition and bodyweight logging, historical entries, and charts into one interface, so users can follow changes in their fitness data without working directly with API endpoints. Building it helped me connect a desktop frontend to a REST API while practicing interface design, event handling, and organizing a larger Java project.

title: MacroCoachAPI
summary: A Python API for nutrition logging and weekly fitness insights.
description: MacroCoachAPI is a Python backend I developed to store and analyze nutrition and bodyweight data. Built with FastAPI, SQLite, SQLAlchemy, and Pydantic, it provides endpoints for logging daily entries, retrieving historical records, and generating insights from recent trends. I also explored how past calorie intake and weight changes could inform future targets, making the project a practical introduction to database design, validation, and REST API development.

title: StatSide
summary: A sports analytics app for exploring and comparing stats.
description: StatSide is an in-progress soccer analytics website focused on making player and team statistics easier to explore. I'm building the frontend with React and Vite, using reusable components and a clean layout to present sports data. The longer-term plan includes API-Football integration, search, side-by-side comparisons, and saved favorites. It's a way for me to combine my interest in soccer with practice in frontend architecture and data-driven web applications.

title: CorBrawl
summary: A Java action game with combat, hazards, and an infinite world.
description: CorBrawl is an early top-down action game prototype I created in Java Swing. The current version explores keyboard movement, mouse aiming, a camera that follows the player through a scrolling world, and basic environmental hazards. The project gave me hands-on experience with game loops, rendering, input handling, and object-oriented organization, while providing a foundation for expanding the gameplay over time.

title: Personal Website
summary: My personal portfolio, built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
description: This portfolio is a website I designed and built from scratch with HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript. It features responsive layouts, custom SVG details, subtle scroll and hover animations, and a searchable, category-filtered project collection powered by JSON. I focused on keeping the design personal and professional while refining accessibility, performance, and a consistent code structure across pages. It's also an ongoing place to experiment with frontend design as I learn new techniques.

title: List Manager
summary: A tabbed desktop app for organizing lists.
description: A Python Tkinter application for managing multiple lists in separate tabs. Users can add, edit, delete, and reorder items, with their lists automatically saved to JSON so they remain available between sessions.

title: Expense Tracker
summary: A command-line tool for recording and reviewing expenses.
description: A command-line expense tracker built in Python to make recording and reviewing spending straightforward. It supports adding, updating, and deleting entries, saves records in JSON, and displays expenses in an easy-to-read table.

title: Hangman Trivia
summary: A trivia and hangman game with API-sourced questions.
description: A Tkinter game that combines trivia questions with hangman-style gameplay. It fetches questions from an external API and updates the interface as players submit answers, giving me practice with API requests and interactive GUI state.

title: Fitness Tracker
summary: An analyzer for MyFitnessPal exports and nutrition trends.
description: I built this Python command-line tool to explore my own fitness data exported from MyFitnessPal. It summarizes nutrition, weight, and exercise records and uses Matplotlib charts to make calorie intake, macronutrients, and trends easier to understand. The project helped me practice working with real-world data and turning raw records into useful visualizations.

title: Mediocre Banker
summary: A simple banking simulator with transaction logs.
description: A Python command-line banking simulator supporting deposits, withdrawals, and transfers between accounts. It organizes account data into folders and stores dated transaction logs as JSON files, providing practice with file handling and program state.

title: F1 Stats Visualizer
summary: An F1 statistics explorer with charts and standings.
description: A Python data visualization project built around my interest in Formula 1. It retrieves racing statistics from an external API and uses Matplotlib to explore standings and driver or team performance through charts. I used it to practice consuming API data and presenting statistics in a more visual, understandable format.

title: Travel Planner
summary: A command-line itinerary and packing checklist tool.
description: A Python command-line planner for organizing trips, checking travel date ranges, and generating packing checklists using simple rules. It saves itineraries to files so trip details can be referenced later.
